title: How Long a Habit Takes Is the Wrong Question
title_alternatives: 21, 66, 59: Every Habit Number Is a Survivorship Statistic
The Habit Timeline Nobody Can Give You
description:
Every habit number you have heard is a median of the people who finished.

21 days comes from a 1960 book by a plastic surgeon describing self-image after surgery. 66 days describes the shape of an automaticity curve, not a deadline. 59 days comes from a 2024 systematic review in which only four of twenty studies measured timing at all, and only 23% of participants ever reached the threshold.

This video traces each number to its source, shows why the spread matters more than the midpoint, and replaces the question with one you can actually act on.

Narrated with a synthetic voice (Kokoro-82M, Apache-2.0 weights). No third-party footage, music, or cloned voice is used; every visual is generated by code.

Nothing here is medical advice.
